plain_what: A language model built as a stack of layers. Most layers carry a running memory that a learned four-number spinner (a unit quaternion) rotates and fades at each word; a few look back over earlier words. It was the main trained model, 7 to 214 million parameters, until the rules banned most of its arithmetic.
how_it_works: Layers repeat in a pattern such as rrarra: r is a recurrence layer, a is a read layer, each followed by a feed-forward block in a residual stream with RMS normalisation. Recurrence: lanes of four channels hold a quaternion state h. Per token, h_t = lambda_t * (u_t * h_(t-1)) + sqrt(1 - lambda_t^2) * c_t, where * is the Hamilton product, u_t is a unit quaternion computed from the input (starting at identity), lambda_t is a gated decay with timescales spread from 2 to about 1,000 tokens, and c_t is a width-4 causal convolution of the input. Read layers: attention over earlier positions with a dot, Euclidean (l2) or Lorentz hyperbolic-distance score. Feed-forward: SwiGLU with dense projections. Optional parts: a copy-pointer head, a product-key memory that replaces an MLP or the last read (split the query into halves, keep the top-k sub-keys per side, join, gather value rows), and flock or starling rank reads. It is trained in float on GPU (AdamW) at 7M, 19.9M, 29M and 214M parameters, then exported to 4-bit grouped weights and served by the D11 integer engine. Measured arithmetic of the 29M stack: MLP 39.6%, recurrence projections 31.0%, reads 16.6%, output head 7.4%, the quaternion rotations 0.05% (16,128 multiplies per token out of 30.3M); the geometry sits inside dense projections.
geometry: Unit quaternions (S3) as the recurrence transport, with an optional snap of each rotation to the nearest unit icosian (2I); matched abelian U(1) control; Lorentz (hyperboloid) read score; optional fixed H4 and E8 codebooks for product-key memory (never run); in the earlier dense R4/Spin references, attention was reproduced exactly in cumulative R4/Spin/H4 frames.

status_reason: PARKED: the form actually trained (softmax reads, sigmoid and SiLU gating, dense matmul) is banned by D23/D25/D30 and never met the M1 bars (memory 20/40 vs 34; served 1.20-1.24 vs 0.90 BPB, docs/labs/d11-serving-2026-10-10). Its quaternion transport was KEPT (docs/integration/transport-attribution-d1-2026-09-28.md); a lawful 24-kernel extract is built but untrained.
reopen_conditions: A new D37 pre-registration with TEST FITNESS: FIT that rebuilds the stack from lawful parts only (Hamilton-gate feed-forward, geometric or dyadic recurrence, flock/relation or rank-margin reads; no softmax, sigmoid, SiLU, GELU or GEMM), in its own scanned module, with the training hold released by the owner.
It reports the export gap on the same evaluator as the float score and targets M1 criterion 2 (D11 served at or below 0.90 BPB on the chat held-out stream).
At least 2 seeds or 200 fresh rows (D22), compared only with prior native rungs and lawful count references (D28: no transformer controls).
The dense hotspots the audit found (MLP 39.6%, recurrence projections 31.0%) are replaced by addressed or exact-geometry reads and shown to move tokens per second on the product path (D5-b).

Optional, as the spinor/quaternion adapter in step 4 of the post-dose optimization path (docs/labs/optimization-path-2026-10-18/README.md): conditional, float offline, discretized serving, measured-ceiling entry only.

rule_compat.D11: The trained stacks were exported (GPTQ, 4-bit) and served bit-exactly by the D11 engine: d11 minus d10 NLL 0.0, max logit difference 0 (docs/labs/d11-serving-2026-10-10/README.md). But every weight is read every token (about 30.2M parameters per token at 29M), which D5-b calls non-compliant, and the engine's attention uses exp-table masses.
rule_compat.D23: The trained form contains banned content: softmax attention reads, a sigmoid gate on the decay, a softplus-parametrised decay rate, SwiGLU (SiLU), and a GELU output gate. The D29 split moved 33 kernels carrying softmax, sigmoid, softplus, tanh-GELU, exp/log and wmma/mma out of every compiled module (docs/labs/d29-module-split-2026-10-13/README.md).
rule_compat.D30: Dense projections and MLPs are matrix multiplication, and the old kernel source used tensor-core contractions; both are banned anywhere, including training.
rule_compat.D32_D37: D37 allows float forward, gradients and optimizers offline, but only geometric and lawful ops, in a separately scanned module, with the export gap reported. Measured historical export gaps: 0.00883 to 0.01944 BPB (19.9M, identical positions) and +0.0257 nats GPTQ on the 7M stack.

experiments.result: The served model is a transformer-shaped dense stack with a quaternion-mixed residual; the geometry is 0.05% of the arithmetic and the Lorentz score, zeta phases, primes and exact store are not in the trained base.

never_tested: A stack built only from lawful parts (Hamilton-gate feed-forward, dyadic recurrence, rank or flock reads) and trained at the scale where this one reached 0.877 BPB: the 24-kernel extract is qualified at finite controls only.
Cycle 5 product-key memory layers with fixed H4 and E8 codebooks: the experiment is NOT_RUN and was held (docs/integration/memory-layers-cycle5-2026-09-27.md).
Trained-in 2I or E8 read addresses with magnitude carried: until the geometric toolbox record of 2026-09-28 nothing had been trained in, and the snapped-training route (#1912) closed only one recipe.
Lorentz reads in the 29M chat base: it trains with read=l2 (the flat ablation control), so the hyperbolic read's contribution at chat scale is unmeasured.
A 10-layer stack trained on a data set larger than the 82M-token chat-v0-p2 split (none was reachable, #1913).
A fair energy measurement: the only figures are the truncated captures and the 4.3x-worse per-product emulation (see lut-serving).
A step-matched control for the addressed-memory half-step 22/40 reading.
failed_only_on_configuration: #951 4.4416% vs 5%: one layer of a frozen SmolLM2 with a memory adapter, nine held-out positions; says nothing about a trained stack.
#1017 sealed NLL 1.5728 vs 1.50: one 7.16M model at 150M tokens; the record keeps attention and calls it NLL-only.
#1057 98.52% vs the strict 99% target is near-target, not a failed mechanism (record wording).
Export gap 0.0257 vs 0.02 and the Hadamard / E8P codecs: rounding recipes on a dense float stack, not on the integer boundary itself.
Addressed memory 19/40 vs 27/40 and the lean +0.095 BPB: particular codebook sizes and placements of a lookup memory trained at the anchor's own step count.
214M 1.0966 vs 0.9607: a data-mixture finding on different protocols, not a verdict on scale.
v5 10/40: the model had no memory operator at all, per the record's own qualifier.

D20 3-seed contest: the geometric mean was higher (0.6689 vs 0.2534) but one seed at 0.0073 fell below every control seed, so the pre-registered rule returns INCONCLUSIVE; it exposes a seed-reliability problem, not a loss.
open_questions: Which of the stack's dense blocks can be replaced by exact geometry or addressed reads without losing the 0.877 BPB class, in tokens per second on the product path?
Why did the geometric read fail on one seed and succeed on two in the D20 contest, and does a better initialisation remove the seed gap?
Is the quaternion transport still load-bearing once its projections are lawful (Hamilton gate, spin-native weights)?
What does the label 'P/Q' mean exactly in the Step 8 arms, and which 214M variants are worth preserving beyond bases/geo-214m-e448de86?
How much of the 31/40 v4 memory result at 214M came from capacity rather than data (the 214M model was weaker on BPB than a 7M one)?

rank-margin: the lawful hinge objective that replaces cross-entropy for this stack
